page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average tier, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, are positioned in the weaker tier. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with uncached read speeds at 28.42 GB/sec and write speeds at 21.13 GB/sec.

From a workload perspective, the c3-standard-4 is suited for general-purpose applications that do not require high parallel processing power or massive memory footprints. It performs adequately in single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing, as well as static web serving, which reached a throughput of 6.68 GB/sec. It is less optimal for heavy database operations, software compilation, or multi-threaded decompression due to its lower multi-core and memory performance profiles.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core execution, supported by Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), though multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the weaker tier. The instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and light single-threaded processing tasks rather than intensive database operations or parallelized computing.
